ch4_opening.speaker: narrator
ch4_opening.text: The killing has spread to every hill. Joseph's storage room, behind the cupboard, now holds people whose names were written in someone's book.

ch4_opening.speaker: joseph
ch4_opening.text: We need food, blankets and water in there before they sleep. Take the food from the shelf, the blankets from the chest. The water is in the barrel in the yard.

ch4_opening.speaker: joseph
ch4_opening.text: The men walk past the gate all night. They can see through the bars. Keep low in the yard, and wait until the path is empty.

ch4_opening.speaker: joseph
ch4_opening.text: Mama Beata will come to the back window after dark. She is bringing medicine.

choices.text: "How long can we keep them hidden, Papa?"

ch4_opening.speaker: joseph
ch4_opening.text: One night at a time, Emmanuel. Nobody can promise more than that.

ch4_joseph.speaker: joseph
ch4_joseph.text: One thing at a time. Quietly.

ch4_take_food.speaker: narrator
ch4_take_food.text: Emmanuel fills a basket from the shelf: beans, a little flour, the last of the bananas.

ch4_take_blankets.speaker: narrator
ch4_take_blankets.text: Two blankets from the chest. They smell of smoke and of home.

ch4_take_water.speaker: narrator
ch4_take_water.text: The rain barrel is nearly full. Emmanuel fills the jerrycans as quietly as water allows.

ch4_beata.speaker: narrator
ch4_beata.text: A soft scratch at the shutter. Emmanuel opens it a hand's width.

ch4_beata.speaker: beata
ch4_beata.text: Here. Medicine: bandages, iodine, a few tablets for fever. It is all I could find.

ch4_beata.speaker: emmanuel
ch4_beata.text: Is there any news of Olivier?

ch4_beata.speaker: beata
ch4_beata.text: Not yet. But no bad news either. The people I trust are still looking.

ch4_beata.speaker: beata
ch4_beata.text: Emmanuel, they are searching houses now. Not every night, not every house. But they are coming closer.

ch4_beata.speaker: beata
ch4_beata.text: Thank me when this is over.

ch4_beata.speaker: beata
ch4_beata.text: Because I have sold salt to every family on this hill for twenty years. Every one of them. I will not choose now which ones deserve to live.

ch4_beata_wait.speaker: narrator
ch4_beata_wait.text: The shutter is closed. Mama Beata will come when it is fully dark.

ch4_aline_supplies.speaker: aline
ch4_aline_supplies.text: You brought all of this? Without being seen?

ch4_aline_supplies.speaker: aline
ch4_aline_supplies.text: Then we ration it. A little water every few hours. The blankets for Gasana and the children first. I'll keep the medicine; I know how to use it.

ch4_aline_supplies.speaker: aline
ch4_aline_supplies.text: I'm not a doctor. I'm a medical student hiding in a storage room. But I'll be a doctor one day. I promised you, didn't I?

ch4_aline_supplies.speaker: aline
ch4_aline_supplies.text: News of my brother. And for this to be over.

ch4_aline_supplies.speaker: narrator
ch4_aline_supplies.text: Aline hands out the blankets. Gasana takes his with both hands, like a gift.

ch4_aline.speaker: aline
ch4_aline.text: Every time I hear footsteps, I think it's Olivier. And every time, I hope it isn't. Because if it's him, it means he's out there alone.

ch4_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch4_gasana.text: Forty years I have been your father's neighbour. I never thought I would live in his storage room. I never thought I would be grateful to.

ch4_solange.speaker: solange
ch4_solange.text: I came from the next hill. I ran when they came, and I kept running until your father opened his door.

ch4_solange.speaker: solange
ch4_solange.text: I don't know where my parents are. I keep telling myself they ran too.

ch4_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch4_claudine.text: Eric hasn't spoken all day. He just holds my hand. Thank you for bringing us here, Emmanuel.

ch4_mats.speaker: narrator
ch4_mats.text: Emmanuel rolls up the extra sleeping mats and pushes them under the bench. A house with one old man and his son needs only two.

ch4_cups.speaker: narrator
ch4_cups.text: Seven cups on the table. Emmanuel washes five and puts them away. Two cups. Two people.

ch4_into_room.speaker: joseph
ch4_into_room.text: Someone is coming up the path. Several men. Go in, Emmanuel. Stay with them.

ch4_into_room.speaker: joseph
ch4_into_room.text: Whatever you hear, do not make a sound. Do not come out. Not for anything.

ch4_farewell.speaker: narrator
ch4_farewell.text: Long after the footsteps have gone, the cupboard slides back. Mama Beata is at the back window.

ch4_farewell.speaker: beata
ch4_farewell.text: They will search every house tomorrow, and this one first. They must leave tonight.

ch4_farewell.speaker: beata
ch4_farewell.text: There is a way through the valley, past the old road, to the river. On the other side, people say, there is shelter. I will take you to the start of the path myself.

ch4_farewell.speaker: joseph
ch4_farewell.text: No. If this house is empty, they will look for you. If I am here, they will look at me.

ch4_farewell.speaker: joseph
ch4_farewell.text: No. Your place is with them now. That is what I raised you for.

ch4_farewell.speaker: joseph
ch4_farewell.text: I know you will try. That is enough for me.

ch4_farewell.speaker: narrator
ch4_farewell.text: Joseph holds his son for a long moment, the way he did when Emmanuel was small.

ch4_farewell.speaker: joseph
ch4_farewell.text: Take care of each other. All of you. Quietly, and together.

ch4_farewell.speaker: narrator
ch4_farewell.text: Then he opens the back door into the dark.
